description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:730-738 (query_objects) vs backend.rs:703-709 (get_changes) and backend.rs:745-757 (query_changes).

  fn query_objects<O>(...) -> impl Future<Output = Result<QueryResult, Self::Error>> + Send;
  fn get_changes<O>(...)   -> impl Future<Output = Result<ChangesResult, BackendChangesError<Self::Error>>> + Send;
  fn query_changes<O>(...) -> impl Future<Output = Result<QueryChangesResult, BackendChangesError<Self::Error>>> + Send;

The asymmetry is: query_objects has no path to surface "I cannot satisfy this query" as a typed error. Every error becomes Self::Error → wrapped by handle_query (crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs:205) into JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string()) → serverFail on the wire. That's the same leak path as JMAP-wlip.2 but it ALSO loses information.

Real cases where /query has typed failure modes RFC 8620 §5.5 + §6.4 allow but this signature can't express:
- The backend's search index is rebuilding and cannot serve this filter yet → RFC 8620 has no specific error for this, but the deployment may want to return `cannotCalculateChanges`-style behaviour (force a full refetch). With BackendChangesError it could emit TooManyChanges { limit: 0 }; with bare Self::Error it cannot.
- The filter exceeds backend complexity limits → RFC 8620 §6.4 specifies `unsupportedFilter`. With BackendChangesError the variant could be added; with bare Self::Error the backend has to fake it through serverFail.
- The sort property is not indexable → RFC 8620 §6.4 specifies `unsupportedSort`. Same problem.

The QueryError envelope shape could be:

  #[non_exhaustive]
  pub enum BackendQueryError<E> {
      UnsupportedFilter,
      UnsupportedSort,
      Other(E),
  }
  impl<E: Error> From<BackendQueryError<E>> for JmapError { ... }

…which mirrors BackendChangesError's pattern at backend.rs:366-432. handle_query then becomes:
  .await.map_err(JmapError::from)  // same shape as handle_changes

Same fix applies to a `BackendSetError` extension for /set methods if there's a deficiency there too (this bead is /query-focused; /set is already covered by BackendSetError).

Inconsistency cost to callers: a backend implementor must read the doc to know "Why does query_objects have a different error envelope than get_changes? Is this intentional or a bug?" The answer is "intentional but suboptimal" and the difference forces hand-coded JmapError construction inside backend impls instead of `From` plumbing.
title: JmapBackend::query_objects returns Result<_, Self::Error> while get_changes/query_changes return Result<_, BackendChangesError<Self::Error>> — inconsistent error envelopes hide /query failure modes
